channel.title: Problems with tirdad module
channel.description: The system says I have tirdad installed. It says that there is a module. In the past, it has even loaded the module --supposedly. At this point, given the information I have thus far, I could not tell you which version of tirdad I have because I get conflicting information. The closest to "fact" seems to be dkms which claims 0.3.5 -1. I am no stranger to the command line but I have gone around in enough circles that it is time to ask for help. My installation is nothing crazy and the only thing that is not "stock" is the sysmaint split which is, for the time being, uninstalled for convenience while building the system.

item.title: Problems with tirdad module
item.dc:creator: arraybolt3
item.description:
I’m not sure what problem you’re running into from this description. Does tirdad appear to not be updating? Is an error message related to it appearing in systemcheck? Is there some other issue with it?

ASmith:

The closest to “fact” seems to be dkms which claims 0.3.5 -1.

Looking at tirdad/debian/changelog at master · Kicksecure/tirdad · GitHub as of today:

tirdad (0:0.3.5-1) unstable; urgency=medium

  * New upstream version (local package).

 -- Patrick Schleizer <adrelanos@whonix.org>  Mon, 17 Aug 2026 04:28:30 +0000

So that looks like the latest available version. The 0: missing at the start is normal.
